newsitem.title: CROATIA: Hotelier stocks propel Croatian OTC market up.
newsitem.headline: Hotelier stocks propel Croatian OTC market up.

text.p: A steep rise in hotelier stocks propelled the Croatian over-the-counter market up to a record high in the week to September 27, the Varazdin OTC market said on Monday.
"This rise was some 50 percent stronger than the one last spring," analyst Domagoj Grabovac told Reuters.
The market's 10-stock index VIN rose 3.63 percent to hit an all-time high of 7,282 points on September 26 but eased to end the week at 7,254.
Grabovac said the rise would have been even more pronounced if some other fast growing company stocks, such as confectioner Kras, were included.
A previous VIN record was 7,073 points in June.
The Varazdin market deals in stocks which do not meet requirements for a full bourse listing, as well as some paid or unpaid shares from employee buyouts in partly privatised firms.
Eleven of 17 traded firms rose, only two fell and four close unchanged from a week earlier.
The biggest gainer was hotelier Riviera from Porec, rising 33.33 percent to 40 German marks a share on volume of 2,370.
Textile firm Varteks was the bigger of two losers, falling 5.0 percent to 19 marks. It sold 2,763 units
The most actively traded, food processor Podravka, rose 7.7 percent to 71 marks with 22,517 shares sold for a turnover of 1.5 million marks.
Total weekly volume was up at 41,300 shares with turnover at 2.6 million marks, including the market's outpost in Osijek. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
